title: Tikkurilan osaamiskampusalueen Oppilaitoskorttelin tilaturvallisuuskokonaisuuden urakka ja palvelut
description: Tikkurilan osaamiskampusalueen Oppilaitoskorttelin tilaturvallisuuskokonaisuuden urakka ja palvelut Hankinnan kohteena on Tikkurilan osaamiskampusalueen Oppilaitoskortteli -uudisrakennuksen tilaturvallisuusjärjestelmäkokonaisuuden urakka ja takuun jälkeisen korjaus-, huolto- ja ylläpitopalveluiden toimitus. Hankinta sisältää tilaturvallisuusjärjestelmien ja niiden hallinta-alustan toimittamisen ja käyttöönoton käyttökuntoon saakka, sekä korjaus-, huolto- ja ylläpitopalvelut. Hankinta sisältää seuraavat järjestelmätoimitukset: - Kulunvalvontajärjestelmä - Kameravalvontajärjestelmä - Rikosilmoitinjärjestelmä - Ovipuhelinjärjestelmä - Henkilöturvajärjestelmä - Hätäkuulutusjärjestelmä - Lukitusjärjestelmä - VIRVE-verkko - Järjestelmäkokonaisuuden hallinta-alusta Oppilaitoskortteli -uudisrakennus tulee sijoittumaan Tikkurilan osaamiskampuksen alueelle lähelle Tikkurilan asemaa, osoitteeseen Jokiniemenkatu 1, 01370 Vantaa. Oppilaitoskortteli -uudisrakennus käsittää opiskelutilat noin 2600 opiskelijalle viidestä eri oppilaitoksesta: Vantaan Ammattiopisto Variasta, Tikkurilan lukiosta, Tikkurilan iltalukiosta, Vantaan aikuisopistosta ja Vantaan Musiikkiopistosta. Lisäksi henkilökuntaa on noin 300. Oppilaitoskorttelissa on kellarikerroksen lisäksi maan päällä kuusi opetustoiminnan kerrosta ja IV-konehuonekerros. Hankesuunnitelman mukainen laajuus on 25 200 brm2 ja tontin pinta-ala on noin 7900 m2. Kohde on toiminnaltaan, sijainniltaan ja turvallisuusympäristöltään poikkeuksellisen vaativa. Kohteen tilaturvallisuudessa on huomioitava useat käyttäjäryhmät, jotka käyttävät kiinteistöä eri tavoin ja eri ajankohtina, sekä laaja määrä julkisia tiloja, joihin on kulku pääsisäänkäynnin kautta. Lisäksi järjestelmätoimituksissa on huomioitava tilojen muuntojoustavuus sekä toimitettavien järjestelmien skaalautuvuus tulevaisuudessa myös muihin kiinteistöihin ja uusille käyttäjäryhmille. Hankittavaan urakkaan kuuluu 24 kuukauden takuuaika ja pidennetyt takuuajat. Työssä noudatetaan urakkatoimituksen osalta YSE 1998 -ehtoja, sekä palveluiden osalta JYSE-palvelut 2025 -ehtoja tarjouspyynnössä ja sopimuksessa esitetyin poikkeuksin. Tilaturvallisuusurakka toteutetaan rakennusurakan alistettuna sivu-urakkana, jossa projektinjohtourakoitsijana (pääurakoitsija ja -toteuttaja) toimii YIT rakennus Oy.,

title: Technical Assessment and Cost-Benefit Analysis on Fuel Storage Tank Systems Life Cycle (Installation, Maintenance and Removal)
description: Amendment # 001 raised to amend the solicitation closing date and answer questions from industry. Amended the UNSPSC of the Tender Notice. Offers. Canada is seeking offers from Offerors to provide a Technical Assessment and Cost-Benefit Analysis on Fuel Storage Tank Systems Life Cycle (Installation, Maintenance and Removal) to Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) as described in Annex Statement of Work. The technical assessment and cost-benefit analysis will evaluate various options for the installation, maintenance, and decommissioning of storage tank systems and how they align with current industry practices in Canada. The analysis must identify associated environmental impacts, resource requirements, benefits, challenges, and operational and policy risks such as regulatory misalignment, compliance barriers, or unintended socioeconomic consequences that go beyond environmental considerations. This includes considerations for both the regulated community and key industry stakeholders such as certified installers, professional engineers, project managers, consultants, and manufacturers. The Contractor must assess the most common and practical procedures currently used in the industry for the installation, maintenance, including leak detection options, and decommissioning of various types of storage tank systems located in Canada. The Contractor must review applicable requirements under the National Fire Code of Canada (NFCC), CSA B139 Installation Code for Oil-Burning Equipment, the CCME Code of Practice, and any other authority having jurisdiction (AHJ) with best requirements for protecting against fuel contamination. Term. The period of the Contract is from date of Contract (est. October 1, 2026) to December 31, 2027, inclusive. Resource Categories The resource categories (roles)* required are as follows: 1. Licensed Professional Engineer 2. Petroleum Storage Tank System Technician 3. Petroleum Storage Tank Systems Compliance Specialist 4. Project Manager *As part of its proposed Project Team, the Offeror can propose the same resource for any of the resource categories required, with the exception that the Licensed Professional Engineer cannot be the same proposed resource as the Petroleum Storage Tank System Technician. Note to Offerors: The proposed resource title (resource categories) in Annex Technical Criteria are descriptive labels intended solely to indicate the nature of the expertise required. They do not represent formal occupational classifications or restrict the number of resources proposed, the allocation of responsibilities, or the manner in which an Offeror structures its Project Team.

title: Housekeeping Services for Buildings and Infrastructure at the Cap-Tourmente National Wildlife Area (CTNWA)
description: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) invite qualified suppliers to submit a bid for the provision of housekeeping services for the buildings and infrastructure located at the Cap-Tourmente National Wildlife Area (CTNWA) in Saint-Joachim, Quebec. The services include regular and periodic cleaning of various administrative, operational, and public facilities, including offices, workshops, interpretation centres, and sanitary facilities, in order to maintain high standards of cleanliness, hygiene, and sanitation. Mandatory Site Visit: A mandatory site visit will take place on September 17, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. Bidders must be represented by at least one authorized representative for the entire duration of the visit. Participation will be confirmed through the mandatory signing of the attendance register upon arrival and departure. Bidders who do not attend the visit or fail to sign the attendance registers will be deemed non-compliant and their bids will not be considered. The initial contract period will be from December 1, 2026, to March 31, 2028, with four (4) one-year option periods that may be exercised at Canada's discretion.

title: Chemical Residue and Allergen Testing in and on Food Products for Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA)
description: AMENDMENT TO CLOSING TIME: Please disregard the Ariba Discovery posting response deadline closing time and Buyandsell posting closing time. All required supporting documentation and bid submission must be submitted by 2026-10-02 at 2 p.m. EST. All bids submitted after 2 p.m. EST will result in the bid being declared non-responsive. This solicitation is for the requirement of analytical and laboratory services for the testing of chemical contaminants and/or allergens in foods, food crops, and tissues of food animals for the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA). Multiple contracts will be established as a result of this solicitation. The requirement is divided into two distinct parts. Part A: Categorized by commodity/food group for a total of 7 food groups (Dairy, Eggs, Fish & Seafood, Fresh Fruit & Vegetables, Honey, Meat, and Processed Products). Part B: Categorized by testing programs for a total of 24 programs (including 3-MCPD, Arsenic, BPA, Alternaria, Benzopyrene, etc.). An Offeror may submit an offer for one or multiple food groups in Part A and/or for one or more testing programs in Part B. Contracts awarded to bidders for multiple food groups and/or programs will be consolidated into a single contract. The full Submission of Offers and annexes can only be accessed and downloaded when logged into your SAP Ariba account and your Government of Canada profile has been approved by SAP Ariba. For technical support with SAP Ariba, please contact the CanadaBuys Service Desk.

title: Germany – Track construction works – Schadschwellenprogramm GoS Südost 2027
description: Im Rahmen mehrerer Einzelmaßnahmen wird auf einer insgesamten Streckenlänge von ca. 115 km in den 6 Netzen der DB InfraGO AG Region Südost der Wechsel von Schadschwellen durchgeführt. Hauptsächlich werden defekte Betonschwellen mittels Großmaschinentechnik ersetzt. An Bahnhöfen und Engstellen wird ein konventioneller Schwellenwechsel angestrebt. Mit dem Einbau der neuen Schwellen erfolgt mindestens auch eine Bettungsreinigung. Alle Arbeiten werden mit minimalen Betriebsunterbrechungen durchgeführt. Das Projekt zielt darauf ab, drohende La-Stellen in 2027/28 zu vermeiden und damit wesentlich zur Netzstabilität und Verfügbarkeit in der Region Südost beizutragen.

title: France – Computer-related services – Mise à disposition en mode SAAS d’une solution numérique de veille et de détection d’éventuels détournements d’usage des données du système d'information de l'ANTENJ et prestations associées ("DADRIM")
description: L’Agence nationale des techniques d'enquêtes numériques judiciaires (ANTENJ) pilote les outils régaliens mis en œuvre en matière d’interceptions de communications électroniques et autres techniques numériques d’enquête. À ce titre, elle met à disposition des magistrats et enquêteurs plusieurs outils informatiques composant le Système d’information des techniques d’enquêtes numériques judiciaires (SITENJ). Dans ce cadre, la présente procédure a pour objet la mise à disposition, par un éditeur de solution standard du marché, d'une solution permettant de surveiller activement l’utilisation illicite éventuelle dans l’espace numérique de données issues du SITENJ qui, en grande majorité, sont strictement soumises au secret de l’enquête ou de l’instruction. Le détail des prestations et fonctionnalités figure dans le dossier de consultation mais la solution doit a minima offrir un service de : 1) veille permanente et de remontée d’information à destination des utilisateurs de l’administration (détection automatisée et alerte) ; 2) recherche active sur demande desdits utilisateurs (détection sur la base des éléments transmis).

title: Ireland – Building installation work – Fire Remediation Works at Rowantree Court, Mullaghmonaghan, Monaghan
description: The project involves the execution of fire remediation works to an existing 24-unit residential development located at Rowantree Court, Mullaghmonaghan, Monaghan, on behalf of the client, Oaklee Housing. The objective of the works is to address identified fire safety deficiencies in order to bring the building into compliance with current fire protection and life safety standards outlined in TGD Part B (Fire Safety) of the Building Regulations and other relevant codes such as IS 3218:2913 for fire alarm systems. The scope of the remediation works includes, but is not limited to: • Installation of fire-stopping systems at service penetrations and wall/floor junctions. • Replacement or upgrade of fire-rated doors, closers, and seals to comply with TGD-B. • Retrofitting of cavity barriers at floor levels in external cavity. • Fire alarm cable rerouting and improvements to service risers and shafts. • Sealing of socket/switch boxes within fire-rated partitions. • General improvement of compartmentation and passive fire protection measures. All works will be undertaken within a live residential environment, requiring a high level of coordination to minimise disruption to residents.

title: Low-Cost Kill Vehicles
description: The Missile Defense Agency (MDA) �Low-Cost Kill Vehicles� solicitation seeks solutions to dramatically decrease the cost of kill vehicles for defense against ballistic and hypersonic threats. This program prioritizes the use of readily available technologies to deliver solutions on a compressed schedule with little to no reduction in performance or reliability. This solicitation seeks to transition concepts into future missile defense interceptors or cost saving upgrades to legacy interceptors. Future interceptors include but are not limited to MDA Low-Cost Interceptor (LCI), Glide Phase Interceptor, Next Generation Interceptor, Navy Modular Missile, etc. Legacy interceptors include standard missile 3 (SM-3), and THAAD. Solutions may include complete kill vehicles or kill vehicle subsystems. description: ***UPDATE 9/2/26: Uploaded Amendment 0001. This Amendment updates Section 00 22 00 to include the Small Business Participation Proposal Worksheet.*** The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Omaha District, hereby announces the solicitation for Gavins Point Intake Crane Rail Replacement. The solicitation will close on 02 October 2026. The solicitation is(Unrestricted and Open to Both Large and Small Business Participation. A Site Visit is scheduled and additional information regarding the site visit is provided in the solicitation via FAR Clause 52.236-27. The site visit is scheduled for 03 September 2026. This project will involve removal and replacement of the Gavins Point Powerhouse Intake crane runway rail located near Yankton, South Dakota. The 80-ton Gavins Point Intake Gantry Crane rail shall be installed and aligned to Crane Manufacturers Association of America, CMAA 70 standards. The total length of the rails is 328 ft x 2 centerline of rail to the powerhouse wall. The work will include an initial survey of the rail alignment, existing grout pocket condition, demolition and removal of existing intake crane rail and components, rail clips, asphalt, base plates, and non-shrink grout. Demolition and removal of the existing concrete anchors will be based on the concrete imaging reports, and the grout pocket condition assessment between each anchor pair along the deck. For bidding purposes, it is assumed 80 percent of the existing anchors will be replaced and all concrete anchors at joint bars will be replaced. The contractor will provide anchors suitable for use in cracked concrete and under seismic loading. Once the rail and hardware are replaced and aligned to the required standards the grout pockets will be filled with two-component aliphatic polyurethane elastomer grout along the full length of the intake crane runway as shown on the drawings. The sequencing of demolition and installation of the crane rails must minimize project time without an operational intake crane and typically progress from one side of the dam to the other with the transfer of the crane from old to new rail during completion of the final rail segment. The Contractor will be required to commence work upon receipt of contract award and complete the work 365 calendar days after receipt of Notice to Proceed, this is subject to change after solicitation issuance. The estimated construction cost of this project is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. The Primary North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this solicitation is 238120, Structural Steel and Precast Concrete Contractors, with a size standard for Small Business of $19M. All questions shall be submitted on ProjNet (ProjNet access, and additional guidance are contained within the solicitation). The Contracting Office is USACE Omaha District, 1616 Capital Ave, Omaha, NE 68102. The Place of Performance is Gavins Point Project, Crofton, NE 68730.

The U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI), Bureau of Reclamation (Reclamation), Lower Colorado Basin, Yuma Area Office, has a requirement for a five (5) year Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract type for Operation and Maintenance (O&M) support services for the Yuma Desalting Plant (YDP) and Water Quality Improvement Center (WQIC). title: Gavins Point Crane Rail Replacement
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Omaha District, hereby announces the solicitation for Gavins Point Intake Crane Rail Replacement. The solicitation will close on 02 October 2026. The solicitation is(Unrestricted and Open to Both Large and Small Business Participation. A Site Visit is scheduled and additional information regarding the site visit is provided in the solicitation via FAR Clause 52.236-27. The site visit is scheduled for 03 September 2026. This project will involve removal and replacement of the Gavins Point Powerhouse Intake crane runway rail located near Yankton, South Dakota. The 80-ton Gavins Point Intake Gantry Crane rail shall be installed and aligned to Crane Manufacturers Association of America, CMAA 70 standards. The total length of the rails is 328 ft x 2 centerline of rail to the powerhouse wall. The work will include an initial survey of the rail alignment, existing grout pocket condition, demolition and removal of existing intake crane rail and components, rail clips, asphalt, base plates, and non-shrink grout. Demolition and removal of the existing concrete anchors will be based on the concrete imaging reports, and the grout pocket condition assessment between each anchor pair along the deck. For bidding purposes, it is assumed 80 percent of the existing anchors will be replaced and all concrete anchors at joint bars will be replaced. The contractor will provide anchors suitable for use in cracked concrete and under seismic loading. Once the rail and hardware are replaced and aligned to the required standards the grout pockets will be filled with two-component aliphatic polyurethane elastomer grout along the full length of the intake crane runway as shown on the drawings. The sequencing of demolition and installation of the crane rails must minimize project time without an operational intake crane and typically progress from one side of the dam to the other with the transfer of the crane from old to new rail during completion of the final rail segment. The Contractor will be required to commence work upon receipt of contract award and complete the work 365 calendar days after receipt of Notice to Proceed, this is subject to change after solicitation issuance. The estimated construction cost of this project is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. The Primary North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this solicitation is 238120, Structural Steel and Precast Concrete Contractors, with a size standard for Small Business of $19M. All questions shall be submitted on ProjNet (ProjNet access, and additional guidance are contained within the solicitation). The Contracting Office is USACE Omaha District, 1616 Capital Ave, Omaha, NE 68102. The Place of Performance is Gavins Point Project, Crofton, NE 68730.

title: On-Ramp_Basic Ordering Agreement Sustainment Track (BOAST) Program
description: ***Questions and Answers Attachment - 18 March 2026*** ***Amendment 0002 - Administrative Change*** ***Amendment 0001 - Administrative Change*** The U.S. Army Contracting Command - Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA) is soliciting requests from qualified and responsible sources to establish Basic Ordering Agreements (BOAs) under the Basic Ordering Agreement Sustainment Track (BOAST) program. This announcement is an "on-ramp" opportunity for interested contractors to compete future orders under the BOAST program. Please note: A Basic Ordering Agreement is not a contract. The award of a BOA does not obligate any Government funds and does not guarantee any future work. Instead, a BOA is a written instrument of understanding that contains pre-negotiated terms, conditions, and pricing methodologies designed to expedite the award of future orders (contracts). 1. Program Description: The BOAST program is a strategic initiative designed to provide an efficient and flexible method for acquiring a wide range of Class IX supplies. These BOAs will cover a broad range of Class IX parts, as defined in DoD Joint Publication (JP) 4-09, Distribution Operations. These parts include repair parts and components including kits, assemblies and subassemblies, and reparable and consumable items required for maintenance support of all Army equipment, excluding medical-peculiar repair parts. title: OCIE-Southeast 3PL
description: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Troop Support, Clothing and Textiles (C&T) Directorate, anticipates the award of a Firm-Fixed Price Service contract with an Economic Price Adjustment (EPA) allowed for standard freight shipments, for Third Party Logistics (3PL) support. This initiative represents the Organization Clothing and Individual Equipment (OCIE) Southeast 3PL Program, a DLA Troop Support initiative to furnish warehousing, storage, inventory management and distribution functions for DLA Troop Support, and its� military customers. The purpose of this initiative is to satisfy customer requisitions for military service C&T items including boots, coats, parkas, helmets, foot lockers, and body armor. The Contractor will not be responsible for requisitioning clothing from the manufacturing community. Rather, DLA Troop Support will procure the replenishment quantities and advise manufacturers to ship directly to the Contractor. The apparel to be stored will be Government owned materiel. The apparel and equipment items to be stored will be Government owned materiel. The current program procedures are as follows: The 3PL Contractor receives apparel and equipment item shipments daily from item manufacturers, other 3PLs and U.S Government supply depots; warehouses the items; and ships directly to C&T customers located both in the Continental U.S. (CONUS) and Outside the Continental U.S. (OCONUS). The acquisition will be conducted in accordance with FAR 15 and FAR part 12 under full and open competition on an unrestricted basis. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. title: Market Research for Survivability, Assured Mobility, and Maneuver Support
description: Market Research for research and development (R&D) efforts on various aspects related to Survivability, Assured Mobility, and Maneuver Support material solutions. The term Survivability encompasses those actions, materiel, and design solutions that give commanders occupant centric survivability through the maturation and integration of technology. Survivability technologies include, but are not limited to, armor, fire protection, hit avoidance, laser protection, countermine, active and passive protection systems, and occupant interior protection. The term "Assured Mobility" encompasses those actions, materiel, and design solutions that give commanders the ability to deploy, move, and maneuver assets where and when they desire, without interruption or delay, to achieve the mission. The imperatives and principles of Assured Mobility are what will enable future forces to have superior situational understanding and, therefore, unsurpassed freedom of movement in global terrain and climate profiles, including, but not limited to, tropical, arid, temperate, continental, and polar. The term "Maneuver Support" encompasses those actions, materiel, and design solutions that give commanders the ability to maintain an unprecedented level of freedom of movement at the tactical, operational, and strategic levels in all environments. Materiel items most relevant to Maneuver Support efforts include survivability, countermine, track and suspension, power management, robotics, bridging systems and combat engineer equipment for the freedom to maneuver through constructed obstacles, unstructured terrain, and for the interrogation of improvised explosive devices (IEDs) and route clearance (mobility and counter-mobility operations).

description: The National Park Service (NPS) is issuing a concessions Prospectus on July 2, 2026, for a concession contract to provide canoe & tube rental with shuttle services, camp store and retail merchandise sales, and firewood sales in the Pulltite area, Upper Current District at Ozark National Scenic Riverways. Attendance is not required in order to submit a proposal.? All parties intending to attend the scheduled site visit must send an email message to Eric Nikkel, Concessions Management Specialist at eric_nikkel@nps.gov, no later than 4:00 p.m. (Central Daylight Time) July 17, 2026, to reserve a spot for the site visit. The email must provide the following information: your name, the name of the organization you are representing, the primary contact for the organization, and the names of the other site visit attendees for your organization. The NPS will provide further information, start time and additional directions by return email message to the organization's identified primary contact.? The Prospectus will be available at https://concessions.nps.gov/subjects/concessions/prospectuses.htm To receive amendments to this Prospectus, please provide Concessions Management Specialist Eric Nikkel, Interior Regions 3, 4, 5, with your contact information (name, email address, and phone number) at eric_nikkel@nps.gov. title: Werkleitungsprojekt Theodosiusweg, Schwyz
description:
Die Gemeinde Schwyz beabsichtigt auf dem rund 160 m langen, privaten Theodosiusweg (Abschnitt Dorfbachstrasse bis Wohnquartier Oberfeld) ein umfassendes Werkleitungsprojekt zu realisieren.


Hauptbestandteil des Projekts ist die gesetzlich erforderliche Einführung des Trennsystems durch den Neubau einer Regenwasserleitung und die Neukonzipierung der bestehenden Mischwasserleitung.

Ebenfalls sind Erneuerungsarbeiten am Trinkwasserleitungsnetz sowie an den Rohranlagen der Telekommunikation und der Wegbeleuchtung geplant.


Die Bauausführung erfolgt unter äusserst engen Platzverhältnissen und in unmittelbarer Nähe zu schützenswerter historischer Bausubstanz. Aufgrund der beengten Verhältnisse und des Umfelds ist ein gespriesster Grabenbau (bis zu 3m Grabentiefe) erforderlich. Zudem müssen bestehende Werkleitungen teilweise vorgängig umgelegt bzw. provisorisch geführt werden, damit die neuen Leitungen erstellt werden können. Die Arbeiten erfordern eine sorgfältige Koordination und etappenweise Abstimmung der verschiedenen Werkleitungen.


Der finale Strassenoberbau erfolgt mehrheitlich in Schwarzbelag. Ein Abschnitt wird entsprechend dem heutigen Erscheinungsbild wieder mit einer traditionellen Natursteinpflästerung ausgeführt.


Die Bauarbeiten sind in drei Hauptetappen geplant. Die Hauszugänge sowie das relevante Wegnetz (Theodosiusweg - St. Karligasse) ist während sämtlichen Bauphasen mittels geeigneter Provisorien für Fussgänger sicherzustellen.

Aufgabenbeschreibung: Die Ausschreibung umfasst Generalplanungsleistungen für die Anpassung der Wasserversorgung inklusive Prüfung des Pumpwerks Sylvenstal in der Staufer-Kaserne Pfullendorf. Die Wasserversorgung der Staufer-Kaserne Pfullendorf war in der Vergangenheit wiederholt von mikrobiologischen Beeinträchtigungen betroffen und soll daher angepasst werden. Hierfür ist zunächst ein Planungskonzept zu erarbeiten. In der Zulaufstrecke soll ein Gebäude für die Unterbringung der Aufbereitungstechnik neu errichtet werden. Die Aufbereitungstechnik wird voraussichtlich eine Druckerhöhungsanlage mit nachgeschalteter Enthärtung (Prinzip: Ionentauscher mit Soletank und nachgeschalteter Dosierung) und UV-C Lichtdesinfektion beinhalten. Das bestehende System der Gebäudeautomation ist zu überprüfen und soweit zu ertüchtigen, dass ein Fernzugriff auf die Pumpe im bestehenden Pumpwerk mit entsprechendem Datenaustausch ermöglicht wird. Die Gesamtkosten der Baumaßnahme betragen ca. 1.620.000 € brutto (geschätzte Kosten der Kostengruppen 200-600 nach DIN 276:2018-12). Planungsbeginn: 12/2026, Baubeginn: 04/2028, Fertigstellung: 08/2029. description: Cette procédure, définie par les art. R. 812-1 et suivants du code de l'énergie, a pour objet la sélection des bénéficiaires du dispositif de soutien pour les filières de production d’hydrogène bas-carbone par électrolyse de l'eau ou d'hydrogène renouvelable sur le territoire français. Les modalités d’octroi de l’aide seront précisées dans le cahier des charges établi à l’issue de la phase de sélection des candidats éligibles à participer à la procédure. L’aide portera sur une durée maximale de 15 ans. Il s’agit de la deuxième vague du régime d’aide SA.101951 ayant fait l’objet d’une décision de la Commission européenne. La procédure de mise en concurrence décrite aux articles R. 812-1 et suivants du code de l'énergie comprend une phase de sélection des candidats éligibles, et une phase de désignation des lauréats, parmi les candidats retenus, pour bénéficier du soutien. À l’issue de la phase de sélection des candidats éligibles, un cahier des charges sera adressé aux candidats en vue de la remise des demandes d’aides finales et de la sélection des Lauréats. Sous réserve des articles L. 2224- 32 et L. 2224-33 du code général des collectivités territoriales, toute personne installée sur le territoire d'un État membre de l'union européenne ou, dans le cadre de l'exécution d'accords internationaux, sur le territoire de tout autre État couvert par un tel accord et désirant construire et exploiter une unité de production sur le territoire français peut participer à cette procédure de mise en concurrence. Cet avis répond aux conditions de l'article R. 812-4 du code de l'énergie. Calendrier prévisionnel de la procédure : les documents de la consultation seront disponibles sur le site de l'ADEME à partir du 01/09/2026. La date limite de dépôt des candidatures est le 02/10/2026 (23h59). La date prévisionnelle de désignation des candidats éligibles à déposer une offre est le 02/11/2026. description: The work under the contract "Support to Eurostat in the domain of Purchasing Power Parities (PPP) for the implementation of the 2027 equipment goods price survey" aims to support Eurostat in the coordination of the PPP surveys on equipment goods and derive PPPs for the component of gross fixed capital formation. This work covers the 41 countries participating in the European Comparison Programme (ECP): EU Member States, EFTA/EEA countries, enlargement countries and the UK. The policy relevance and use of PPPs lie in their role in converting national accounts aggregates into comparable volume measures and in analysing relative price levels across EU countries. This requires high-quality PPP data. These requirements put very strong emphasis on the collection of comparable price data across countries, the validation of the data, and the methodology applied for calculating the PPPs. All according to detailed and agreed time-schedules for the releases of the PPPs. The work on equipment goods prices requires technical knowledge of machinery, electronic and other equipment that is not available at Eurostat. It is, therefore, necessary to ensure high quality standards for the implementation of the contract.

title: Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) Call for Whitepapers for Mission Development Zone (MDZ) Outgrant
description: 1. DESCRIPTION 1.1. Growth of the U.S. Domestic Space industry has resulted in a greater demand for use of real property at U.S. Space Force (USSF) Space Launch Delta 30 (SLD 30), Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) by private and commercial entities to conduct spaceport support, payload processing, hardware manufacturing, testing, logistics, and other space-related activities. Ensuring that United States operators can efficiently process space systems, conduct missions in space, launch, and reenter United States airspace is critical to economic growth, national security, and accomplishing Federal space objectives. 1.2. SLD 30 requests white paper responses from United States Commercial Providers as defined by 51 U.S.C. � 50101(7) engaged in space transportation, spaceport support, spacecraft manufacturing, payload processing, assembly, test, space logistics, or other space-related operations on the buildout of the Mission Development Zone (MDZ). Respondents will offer insights, perspectives, and approaches to obtain real property-use agreements to finance, design, construct, operate, and maintain spaceport infrastructure. Industry insights from whitepaper submissions may be utilized to drive future RFI / RFP announcements issued by SLD 30. Specifically, the MDZ infrastructure is intended to provide critical support services to the Department of War (DoW), commercial spaceflight, and other spaceport users at an undeveloped area located in the southern region of VSFB�s North Base area. Development and utilization of the MDZ will be in support of maximizing spaceport capability and assured access to space to achieve national security objectives. 1.3. Description of Premises is at Exhibit B. Please note that the MDZ is not a space launch complex (launch pad), but rather a flexible development zone dedicated to supporting the broader spaceport ecosystem. This includes, but is not limited to, payload processing, hazardous processing, spaceport logistics, commodity storage, launch and mission control, research and development, spacecraft integration, and administrative/engineering spaces. 1.4. The USSF is gathering market intelligence to determine the feasibility of a future real property outgrant under 10 U.S.C. � 2667 to a commercial space services provider, spaceport support provider, launch service provider (LSP), space infrastructure provider, or other space-related entity to construct spaceport-related support infrastructure. MDZ support infrastructure may include, but is not limited to, the following activities: processing, manufacturing, logistics, and administrative support activities. Data gathered from white paper responses will directly inform the Government in determining optimal MDZ utilization and potential infrastructure requirements to meet Government and industry launch requirements. 1.5. To support its ongoing spaceport capacity expansion, Space Launch Delta 30 (SLD 30) continuously evaluates opportunities and fields requests for new missions. Accordingly, SLD 30 provides discretionary site access and information to prospective partners at any time. Spaceport users and providers responding to this call for whitepapers wishing to view the site may request a property viewing. Please note that scheduling a site visit does not constitute grounds for extending the submittal deadline. 2. CONDITIONS 2.1. This call for whitepapers is not governed by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and is not a Request for Information (RFI), a Request for Proposal (RFP), a Request for Quote (RFQ), nor a solicitation announcement. Content of whitepapers will provide industry insight to assist the Government in scoping, planning, and defining requirements for the proposed MDZ. Content of the whitepapers may assist the Government in generating future contract requirements. Submitters agree and allow the USSF to use the information in the submissions for this purpose. 2.2. This call for whitepapers is issued solely for informational and planning purposes, and the Government is under no obligation to allocate property. The information contained herein is current as of the publication date but subject to change; it is not binding and may be amended in the future. While SLD 30 intends to review submissions, it is under no obligation to do so and reserves the right to cancel or amend the call for whitepapers at its sole discretion. 2.3. No funds are available to fund the whitepaper requested and the Government will not pay or reimburse any costs associated with responding to this request. 2.4. Any future facility where energetic propellants, hazardous materials, and/or ordnance will be used, processed, or stored will require the development of an explosives site plan. To assist the Government in layout and zoning analysis, respondents should outline any anticipated explosive safety arcs, quantity-distance (QD) requirements, or specialized hazard mitigation constraints. 3. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS To assist the U.S. Space Force in scoping and planning for the Mission Development Zone (MDZ), respondents are requested to provide a whitepaper that addresses the following areas. The goal is to gather information on industry needs, operational concepts, and technical requirements to shape the future development of the MDZ. 3.1. Spaceport, Support, and Related Infrastructure Capability. To meet future U.S. Government and commercial space requirements, the USSF seeks to establish robust spaceport support and related infrastructure at VSFB. The MDZ, positioned in the southern area of North VSFB, has been assessed as a potentially viable location for development of infrastructure required for the preparation, operation, and support of launch programs, spacecraft assembly, payload processing, space logistics, and other supporting commercial or industrial activities that enable the spaceport ecosystem. The Government is seeking insights from industry regarding the MDZ layout and planned utilization including types of facilities that would be most beneficial to launch providers in this location. Respondents should provide an assessment with respect to the compatibility of the property with proposed concept of operations. To assist the Government in understanding this capability, respondents should provide a list of all desired facility developments intended to be constructed at the MDZ. 3.2. Payload Processing and Hardware Requirements. A primary objective of the MDZ development is to address current installation capacity constraints regarding payload processing. If a respondent�s concept of operations involves payload or hardware processing, the Government requests specific information regarding requirements to process modern 5-meter-class payloads and next-generation fairings. Respondents should describe necessary facility specifications to include cleanroom class ratings (e.g., ISO 7, ISO 8), overhead crane hook heights, clear span ceiling heights, and projected annual processing throughput. (Note: If a respondent�s proposed operations do not involve payload processing, this section may be omitted). 3.3. Benefit to the Spaceport Ecosystem. Respondents should describe how their proposed operations, facilities, or infrastructure developments will benefit the broader VSFB spaceport ecosystem, the commercial space industry, and U.S. Space Force national security objectives. 3.4. Parcel Selection, Layout Preferences, & Utility Requirements. The MDZ contains roughly 2,100 acres divided into general parcel sizes. The MDZ is located within 5 miles of Vandenberg Airfield with some parcels in the aircraft arrival corridor which will limit building height. To inform the base's Area Development Plan (ADP), respondents are requested to outline their estimated land and utility requirements: Acreage and Parcel Selection: Respondents may address any number of parcels depending on the overall size needed for the discussion of the whitepaper; there is no upper limit to the request.
